tier_reason: BENCHMARKS.md does show a same-machine full ML-KEM-512 session table against LibOQS 0.16.0 on an Apple M5, with LibOQS cmake flags. The public harness, examples/kyber_benchmark.rs, only times moduletto, though. The LibOQS 16.19/20.43 us and Kyber-ref 47.87 us figures are hardcoded constants in it (around lines 2518-2524), taken from a C harness that is not in the repo, and the rustc version is not stated. That makes these first-party numbers without a reproducible baseline run, so the tier is C, not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: ~1.18x faster full ML-KEM-512 session than LibOQS 0.16.0: 13.7-14.1 us vs 16.19 us per session. The page lists moduletto at 0.85x of LibOQS time; the README says ~1.18x. That is ~72,000 vs 61,800 sessions/sec, and moduletto is faster in all three phases: keygen 4.07 vs 4.72 us, encaps 3.84 vs 5.25 us, decaps 5.80 vs 6.22 us. Against the Kyber C reference (47.87 us, carried over from an unre-measured 2026-03-19 run) it is ~3.4-3.5x faster (derived from page data). The page's 2.96x is Kyber-ref vs LibOQS 0.16.0, not vs moduletto.
corrections.baseline: liboqs 0.16.0 (ML-KEM-512, built from source at tag 0.16.0, Release, -O3 -march=native, on aarch64/Apple M5)
corrections.compiler_and_flags: moduletto: rustc (version unstated), Cargo release profile opt-level=3, lto=true, codegen-units=1, panic=abort; sha3 0.10 with the asm feature; timed by examples/kyber_benchmark (10,000 iterations, 100-iteration warmup). LibOQS: cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DOQS_MINIMAL_BUILD=KEM_ml_kem_512 -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-O3 -march=native" from tag 0.16.0, C compiler not named; a source comment says gcc. The LibOQS harness is not published and its results are hardcoded in the example.
corrections.caveats: The margin over LibOQS is small (1.18x), and the author notes LibOQS 0.16.0 is itself 1.26x faster than 0.15.0, so comparisons against older releases overstate the lead. The LibOQS and Kyber-C-reference numbers are hardcoded constants in examples/kyber_benchmark.rs, measured by an unpublished C harness; the Kyber-ref column comes from a 2026-03-19 session and was not re-measured. The ML-KEM-512 KEM itself lives in the benchmark example, not the library API: the crate provides modular arithmetic and NTT. It only became FIPS 203 conformant on 2026-08-11, after ACVP vectors exposed six deviations, including a hardcoded zero implicit-rejection seed. The Platform Notes section at the bottom of BENCHMARKS.md is stale: it describes 2026-03-19, LibOQS 0.15.0 and Apple clang 17. The Cargo.toml repository field points to a nonexistent denjell/circlecimal. The PolyForm Noncommercial license is not OSI-approved, so the code is for study and evaluation only and cannot be used commercially without a separate license.

notes: Downgraded A to C because the baseline numbers are hardcoded constants from a harness that is not in the repo. The Kyber-ref ratio was misattributed. Metadata is correct: license PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0 (confirmed in the LICENSE file), 10 stars, last commit 2026-09-03, not a fork, not archived.

tier_reason: The public Criterion harness, benches/comparison/benches/implementations.rs, runs sntrup, liboqs (oqs 0.11.0 / oqs-sys 0.11.0+liboqs-0.13.0) and PQClean (pqcrypto-ntruprime 0.1.6, avx2 off) in the same process, with pinned versions. RESULTS.md states rustc 1.97.1 on an Apple M2 Max, rustc 1.98.0-nightly on a Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 (Zen 5) pinned to one core, the release profile and the feature choices. Tier A holds.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Current page (Where things stand and the README). On x86_64 (Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, Zen 5) against liboqs's AVX2 build: keypair 106.6 vs 107.9 us (0.99x), encapsulate 10.5 vs 11.5 us (0.91x), decapsulate 8.4 vs 8.4 us (1.00x). That is parity to ~9% faster; round 24 gives 107.81/10.46/8.46 us (0.99x/0.91x/1.01x). Against PQClean clean C on x86 it is 42.7x/22.9x/72.6x faster. On aarch64 (Apple M2 Max, ARM round 3) against liboqs portable C: keypair 683.7 us vs 1.876 ms (2.7x), encapsulate 37.0 vs 52.7 us (1.42x), decapsulate 77.1 vs 91.8 us (1.19x). The record's figures (1.341 ms/50.00/84.52 us on ARM; liboqs 3.3x/2.8x/6.3x ahead on x86) are from the first runs in this append-only log and are outdated.
corrections.baseline: liboqs 0.13.0 via oqs-sys 0.11.0 (sntrup761: AVX2 SUPERCOP-derived backend on x86_64, portable C on aarch64) and PQClean sntrup761 clean C via pqcrypto-ntruprime 0.1.6 (avx2 feature off)
corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.97.1 (aarch64 runs) / rustc 1.98.0-nightly (x86_64 runs), Cargo release profile. Criterion 0.8.1 with a 1 s warm-up, a 3 s measurement window and 10 samples for keygen. oqs 0.11.0 (oqs-sys 0.11.0+liboqs-0.13.0) is built from vendored source; its C build is driven by oqs-sys, with clang 22 on Fedora mentioned for bindgen. pqcrypto-ntruprime 0.1.6 is built without its avx2 feature.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 0 stars; crates.io sntrup v0.4.0 has ~2.8k total downloads
corrections.caveats: On x86_64 the lead over liboqs's AVX2 build is only parity to ~9%. The keypair win depends on an AVX-512 divstep path (Zen 5) that liboqs lacks. With AVX2 only (round 23), keypair was still 1.11x slower than liboqs. The aarch64 wins (2.7x/1.42x/1.19x) are against liboqs and PQClean portable C, because neither has a NEON sntrup761 path. The very large PQClean ratios on x86 are against clean C, since the avx2 feature was deliberately left off. The baseline is liboqs 0.13.0 via oqs-sys 0.11.0, not a current liboqs release. The headline summary table mixes figures from different rounds (keypair 106.6 in the summary vs 107.81 in the round 24 table), and the early x86 run had a concurrent video call. The project has a single maintainer and 0 GitHub stars, but RESULTS.md is an unusually rigorous same-run engineering log.

notes: Confirmed at tier A. The claim was understated: the record's x86 'liboqs wins by 2.8-6.3x' caveat reflects the first x86 run; the latest rounds show parity to slightly faster than liboqs on x86 and 1.19-2.7x faster on aarch64. Metadata is correct: Apache-2.0 OR MIT (dual license files, and the README says 'either of'), last commit 2026-08-05, not a fork, not archived.
